chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Quran was revealed in four quarters: a quarter is regarding us, and a quarter is regarding our enemies, and a quarter is Sunnah and examples, and a quarter is Obligations and regulations.
ai.seo_question: How is the Quran divided into four parts according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) in *Al-Kafi* presents a structural taxonomy of the Quran, categorizing its content into four distinct domains: theological identity (Ahl al-Bayt), eschatological conflict (enemies), moral instruction (parables), and jurisprudence (rulings). This division highlights the comprehensive nature of the Quran as both a spiritual guide and a legal constitution, emphasizing the centrality of the Imams in its interpretation. The classification underscores the Shia view that the Quran's message is inextricably linked to the authority of the Prophet's household.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Quran is Revealed in four (parts) – a quarter is regarding us<sup>asws</sup>, and a quarter is regarding our<sup>asws</sup> enemies, and a quarter is a Sunnah and examples, and a quarter is Obligations and regulations’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu Basir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Holy Quran came in four parts: One fourth is about us (Ahl al-Bayt) one fourth about our enemies, one about traditions and axioms and one fourth about obligations and laws.”
